transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-15 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Morton (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Sam Lee (Stratus Eng Manager), Maria Gomez (Stratus SRE), Tom Nguyen (Stratus Platform)

Summary:
Short scoping call to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing, and how the customer's existing scripts integrate into Redwood's benchmark harness. Main tension: streaming vs non-streaming behavior for their real-time personalization path and how tail latency and cold-starts look under sustained bursts.

Topics:
- Success criteria (p95 latency, throughput targets, cost envelope, quality metrics)
- Harness integration patterns and script adapters
- Streaming vs non-streaming script behavior and fallback policies
- Telemetry, logs and artifacts for acceptance
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Morton: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off in a sec, priya and i will run through the measurement plan and then hand over to you for the script details.
[00:18] Sam Lee: yeah thanks alex, appreciate it. we have a hard deadline — our q4 rollout wants a pilot by mid-july so timeline's kinda tight.
[00:27] Priya Shah: noted. so to frame the POC success, do you have target SLAs? what does success look like from Stratus.
[00:36] Maria Gomez: p95 under 180ms for the personalization API, ideally p50 around 40-50ms, and cost needs to stay within our existing budget or not exceed 2x current. also need audit logs and ability to point traffic at dedicated nodes.
[00:53] Tom Nguyen: and we care about cold start tail latency — if a model spins up we can't have 3s spikes, and KV cache behavior is important for session state.
[01:07] Alex Morton: got it. quick callout — Redwood Dedicaed can be pinned to a model build and gives predictable throughput, also we have streaming endpoints that keep KV in memory for sessionized workloads. note: sometimes the transcript tools output KV as K-V cash, ok.
[01:24] Sam Lee: yeah... we've noticed streaming paths reduce tokens-per-call in practice but add complexity if a request fanouts into multiple tools.
[01:33] Priya Shah: for the harness, the ideal is we run your exact scripts—no synthetic substitution. can you walk through a script and its branching? even pseudocode is helpful.
[01:45] Sam Lee: sure, the main flow is: user request -> mapper -> policy eval -> call to LLM with context ~300 tokens -> postprocess -> personalization lookup -> final. sometimes we call an external re-ranker which is another LLM call. so sometimes it's 1 call, sometimes 3.
[02:05] Maria Gomez: also we have heavy cache hits for returning users, so distribution is about 70% cached one-shot, 20% 2-calls, 10% 3-plus.
[02:14] Priya Shah: perfect that distribution is exactly what we need. for benchmarking we'll need traffic mix and concurrency targets — what's your expected qps in pilot and production?
[02:24] Tom Nguyen: pilot target 150 qps sustained (avg), burst to 800 qps for short periods. production would be ~800 qps sustained.
[02:33] Alex Morton: okay we'll size GPU pool accordingly, but two things: 1) streaming vs non-streaming changes how we batch — streaming keeps latency low but reduces batch granularity, non-streaming lets bigger batch but higher tail. 2) KV cache hit-rate drastically changes cost per token.
[02:49] Sam Lee: can you show an example of what telemetry we’ll get? we need to map to our SLO dashboard.
[02:56] Priya Shah: yes, the harness emits per-request traces, token counts, model version, cpu/gpu utilization, queueing time. we can forward logs to your splunk or send S3 artifacts. we also produce a summary CSV with p50/p95/p99, tokens-per-second, and GPU utilization samples.
[03:18] Maria Gomez: great. one worry — our compliance team insisted on encrypted-at-rest with customer KMS and separation per-tenant logs. does Redwood support KMS integration for Private?
[03:27] Alex Morton: absolutely, Private supports customer KMS/HSM, and we can isolate logs. i'll attach the security pack after this call — it's the standard SOC2/ISO and architecture diagram.
[03:37] Tom Nguyen: thanks. back to harness: do you need us to refactor scripts into callback-based streaming handlers, or can the harness wrap synchronous scripts?
[03:46] Priya Shah: the harness can adapt both. for streaming we prefer a small shim that emits partial tokens as they arrive; for non-streaming we run the whole invocation and measure end-to-end. wrapping synchronous scripts is usually easier but may mask tail token latencies.
[04:05] Sam Lee: hmm ok, some of our legacy code is synchronous. refactoring takes time, so what's the incremental approach?
[04:12] Priya Shah: recommended path: stage 1 run synchronous scripts through harness to get baseline; stage 2 add streaming shim for top 2 latency-sensitive flows; stage 3 full streaming adoption. we can show delta metrics.
[04:24] Alex Morton: i'll add that into the POC milestones. now, about success criteria — can we write them down quickly so we have a shared acceptance test?
[04:33] Sam Lee: yes: 1) p95 <= 180ms for the personalization endpoint under pilot traffic 150 qps sustained; 2) quality parity — auto eval delta <= 3% on our BLEU/ROUGE-like metric; 3) cost per 1M tokens <= $X (we'll share exact budget); 4) security checklist passed (KMS, RBAC, audit logs).
[04:52] Maria Gomez: and operational: ability to fall back to hosted model for 1 minute if dedicated nodes degrade, and a documented rollback plan.
[05:01] Priya Shah: noted. on the benchmarking side we'll run the following matrix: streaming vs non-streaming x cached hits vs cold x 1-call vs 3-call average. that'll give us latency, throughput, and cost contours.
[05:14] Tom Nguyen: what's the expected artifact set from that matrix? we need CSVs and a short writeup.
[05:19] Priya Shah: yes CSVs, GPU traces, and a recommendations doc (quantization, batch settings, suggestion for dedicated pool size). also we'll include guidance for autoscale policy and fallback thresholds.
[05:31] Sam Lee: ok curious about one more thing — do you do model variant fallbacks (e.g., lower-cost model if high latency)? we may accept slight quality drop to save cost.
[05:40] Alex Morton: yes, smart routing supports tiered fallbacks by policy. during POC we'll test fallback to a cheaper 8-bit quantized model and measure quality regressions.
[05:49] Maria Gomez: also need to know how cold starts look with fallback — if primary model is down and fallback spins up, do we get a double spike?
[05:57] Priya Shah: great question. our runtime tries warm pool techniques and keeps lightweight warmups for fallbacks. we'll instrument cold-start tails in the harness. sometimes you'll see a 200-800ms spike depending on model size.
[06:13] Sam Lee: and for the harness - any limitations on our scripts? we call a local redis and an external re-ranker (third party).
[06:21] Priya Shah: harness can proxy external calls or mock them. for correctness we prefer real calls if possible; for scale tests we recommend mock responses to avoid external 3rd-party throttles.
[06:33] Tom Nguyen: lifecycle — what's the POC timeline? you mentioned mid-july for pilot, what are milestones?
[06:39] Alex Morton: proposed timeline: week 1 (now): share scripts and traffic profile; week 2: Redwood runs harness baseline with sync scripts; week 3: streaming shim tests and fallback checks; week 4: run full acceptance matrix and deliver report; pilot kickoff week 5. that lines up with mid-july.
[06:56] Sam Lee: sounds good. can you estimate infra cost to hit 150 qps pilot?
[07:02] Priya Shah: rough order: for their model mix and 70% cache hits, pilot sustained 150 qps maps to a 4-GPU pool (A100-equivalent) with optimized batching. burst capacity needs autoscale to 12 GPUs for short windows. we'll produce a more precise estimate after initial run.
[07:21] Maria Gomez: do you have examples of similar customers and their observed p95?
[07:25] Alex Morton: yes, we ran a retail personalization pilot — p95 was 120ms at 200 qps with streaming and cache hit 65%. i'll anonymize and share highlights.
[07:36] Sam Lee: excellent. final questions: our compliance wants retention controls for logs, can we set retention per-bucket?
[07:43] Alex Morton: yes retention policies can be set and logs exported to your S3 with lifecycle rules.
[07:49] Maria Gomez: and can you sign our data processing addendum (DPA)?
[07:53] Alex Morton: yes, legal will follow up, alex to include contract contact.
[07:59] Priya Shah: ok as next concrete step i'll kick off the harness run with the scripts you share; can you drop them in the shared folder and flag any secrets to obfuscate?
[08:08] Sam Lee: will do. we'll anonymize and upload by tomorrow.
[08:12] Alex Morton: great — to recap next steps in the chat: priya runs harness and shares observability artifacts; alex sends POC scope + security pack; sam uploads scripts and traffic profile.
[08:24] Tom Nguyen: thanks all, we'll be ready on our end for the baseline run.
[08:28] Alex Morton: thanks everyone, talk soon.
